# Structuring a Table

#### Course: HTML Fundamentals for Your First Webpage

## Structuring a Table

You may not fully get the table structure on the first try. So it'll be easier if you remember the basic structure.

Here's how I logically approached the table structure when I first learned HTML:

1. Each table must be wrapped in a container, which is given by the <table> tag.
2. Tables consist of rows and columns. In HTML, we enter data using rows. So, we must then use the table row tag <tr> to start entering data.
3. But tables also consist of columns, and each column needs a header/title. So, the first row of the table must consist of only column headers. This is given by the table head tag <th>.
4. After specifying the column headers, the rest of the rows must consist of data. This is given by the table data tag <td>.

Now, let's apply this logic to create a basic table structure in HTML.

Basic Table Structure

```html
<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Column Header 1</th>
    <th>Column Header 2</th>
    ... ... ...
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Data 1.1</td>
    <td>Data 1.2</td>
    ... ... ...
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Data 2.1</td>
    <td>Data 2.2</td>
    ... ... ...
  </tr>
  ... ... ...
</table>
```
